'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**Response to the [[2021 Kabul airport attack]], [[List of drone strikes in the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan|Drone strikes in the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan]]
***The [[United States Armed Forces|United States]] launches an [[airstrike]] in [[Nangarhar Province|Nangarhar]], killing two [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Khorasan Province|Islamic State]] members and wounding a third. It is reported that one of those killed was planning more attacks in Kabul. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/08/28/politics/isis-k-drone-strike-us-afghanistan/index.html (CNN)]
**Aftermath of [[2021 Taliban offensive]] and [[Fall of Kabul (2021)|Fall of Kabul]]
***Afghan political leader and activist [[Fatima Gailani]], who helped draft a new constitution for Afghanistan and also took part in peace talks with the Taliban, blames exiled former [[President of Afghanistan|Afghan president]] [[Ashraf Ghani]] for the current "chaotic" situation in [[Afghanistan|the country]], and says that [[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Joe Biden]] also contributed by withdrawing troops without a "political settlement" in place. [https://www.dw.com/en/afghan-activist-says-ashraf-ghani-and-joe-biden-caused-misery-and-chaos/a-58998732 (Deutsche Welle)]
***The United States urges the [[Taliban]] to include former president [[Hamid Karzai]] and former Chief Executive [[Abdullah Abdullah]] in the formation of the new inclusive government. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/27/exclusive-taliban-plans-inclusive-caretaker-govt-in-afghanistan (Al Jazeera)]
**[[2021 evacuation from Afghanistan]]
***[[Australia]], [[New Zealand]], [[Norway]] and [[Spain]] end their evacuation flights from [[Hamid Karzai International Airport]] in [[Kabul]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/australian-troops-left-kabul-airport-before-suicide-attack-2021-08-26/ (Reuters)] [https://www.euroweeklynews.com/2021/08/27/spain-ends-the-evacuation-of-people-from-afghanistan/ (''EuroWeekly News'')] [https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/126201780/possibly-hundreds-left-behind-as-new-zealand-afghanistan-evacuation-mission-ends-after-kabul-terror-attack?fbclid=IwAR2EvA1LOOoh3PYfi3S9pYt1ot_jmgbhvo4Ua01IalDUJZP5GJEEZh7lSaI (Stuff)] [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-08-26/norway-halts-kabul-evacuation-says-foreign-minister?fbclid=IwAR0lhxqKr-mmPrgQO3YEHloT4qhkvk7qiFAmEbwzVzSLDPw4_0bFO3pfdsY (''U.S. News & World Report'')]
***Crowds return to the Kabul airport a day after the suicide bombing at the airport. [https://www.voanews.com/us-afghanistan-troop-withdrawal/evacuation-flights-resume-kabul-airport-after-bombings (VOA)]
***[[United States Marine Corps|U.S. Marine]] lieutenant [[Stuart Scheller]] is relieved of his duties after posting a video demanding accountability from military leaders over [[Operation Allies Refuge|the evacuation]]. [https://www.tmz.com/2021/08/28/marine-corp-lt-lieutenant-video-criticizing-military-brass/ (TMZ)] <!-- [https://californianewstimes.com/marine-lt-col-relieved-of-duty-after-criticizing-brass-for-afghanistan-exit/502767/ (''California News Times'')] -->
**[[2021 Kabul airport attack]]
***The death toll from the [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Khorasan Province|ISIL]] [[suicide bombing]] attack at the airport in [[Kabul]] yesterday increases to 175. Three [[United Kingdom|British]] citizens are confirmed to have been killed in the attack. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/27/us-braces-for-more-possible-attacks-after-deadly-kabul-blasts (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**Nineteen civilians are killed during a knife and arson attack by [[Allied Democratic Forces|ADF]] at a village in [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/28/civilians-killed-adf-ugandan-rebels-dr-congo (Al Jazeera)]
**Authorities in [[Uganda]] arrest an [[Islamic extremist|Islamist]] belonging to the ADF for planning a [[suicide bombing]] attack in the country. Police are also investigating if the murders of 21 civilians in the cities of [[Lwengo]] and [[Masaka]] since late July were carried out by ADF terrorists. The victims were killed by knifemen during raids in the night. Thirty-eight suspected have been arrested. [https://allafrica.com/stories/202108280022.html (All Africa)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economy of Zambia]]
**The newly appointed [[Ministry of Finance (Zambia)|Minister of Finance]] ​of [[Zambia]] [[Situmbeko Musokotwane]] says that he has begun to negotiate with the [[International Monetary Fund]] on a $12 billion external debt. Musokotwane says that he is also working with other private funds to which Zambia owes payments. Musokotwane anticipates that Zambia "will not be able to immediately cancel all debts". [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/zambian-president-hichilema-appoints-new-finance-minister-2021-08-27/ (Reuters)]
*[[Economy of Cuba]]
**[[Cuba]] recognizes [[cryptocurrency]] as legal tender, becoming the second nation to do so after [[El Salvador]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/27/cuba-to-recognise-regulate-cryptocurrency-govt-resolution (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
*****According to government data, more than 473 million people have received at least one dose of a [[COVID-19 vaccine]], which amounts to about half of all eligible adults in [[India]]. However, only around 15% of eligible adults have been fully vaccinated against [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-56345591 (BBC)]
*****India reports a single-day record of 10 million doses of the COVID-19 vaccine administered, a level that [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] hailed as a "momentous feat" for the country. [https://www.reuters.com/world/india/india-reports-44658-new-covid-19-cases-last-24-hours-2021-08-27/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****The number of severe COVID-19 patients in Japan surpasses 2,000 for the first time since the beginning of the pandemic. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/08/27/national/coronavirus-tracker-august-27/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]]'s COVID-19 taskforce approves a plan to gradually ease some COVID-19-related restrictions beginning on September 1 that will allow the resumption of [[domestic flight]]s, reopening of shopping malls, restaurants, barbershops, and public parks, as well as allow gatherings of up to 25 people in 29 high-risk [[Provinces of Thailand|province]]s as the number of COVID-19 cases has peaked. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-08-27/thailand-set-to-reopen-malls-restaurants-as-virus-seen-peaked (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports a record 12,920 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to  410,366. The country also surpasses 10,000 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19. [https://vietnamnews.vn/society/1020250/12920-new-covid-19-cases-356-more-deaths-reported-on-friday.html (Viet Nam News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]]
****[[Denmark|Danish]] [[Ministry of Health (Denmark)|Minister of Health]] [[Magnus Heunicke]] announces that the country will lift all COVID-19-related restrictions on September 10 as it considers that the "epidemic is under control" and does not pose "a critical threat to society". The country will also lift the obligation to present an immunity passport in order to attend certain events as more than 70% of [[Danish people|Danes]] are fully vaccinated. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/aug/27/denmark-to-lift-all-remaining-covid-restrictions-on-10-september (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****The [[Italy|Italian]] [[Ministry of Health (Italy)|Health ministry]] signs a decree which moves [[Sicily]] into the "yellow zone" and will reimpose some restrictions such as the [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mask mandate]] both outdoors and indoors and restrict restaurant diners to groups of four beginning on August 30 following an increase of COVID-19 cases. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-08-italy-reimposes-coronavirus-sicily.html (MedicalXpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Poland]]
****[[Poland|Polish]] [[Ministry of Health (Poland)|Minister of Health]] [[Adam Niedzielski]] announces that the Supreme Medical Council has approved [[booster dose]]s of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] for people with a compromised immune system which will be administered beginning on September 1. [https://www.thefirstnews.com/article/medical-council-approves-third-vaccine-for-impaired-immunity-patients-24315 (''The First News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]]
*****[[Scotland]] reports a record 6,835 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-scotland-records-highest-ever-daily-coronavirus-cases-but-no-circuit-breaker-lockdown-planned-12392058 (Sky News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Virginia]], [[Operation Allies Refuge]]
*****[[White House Press Secretary]] [[Jen Psaki]] announces that the [[Federal government of the United States|U.S. government]] has opened a mass vaccination site at the [[Dulles International Airport]] for [[Operation Allies Refuge|arriving]] [[Afghan refugees]]. [https://apnews.com/article/health-coronavirus-pandemic-9b00cce92f9010e5067907f43c21f873 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
****A [[Leon County, Florida|Leon County]] judge strikes down the [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate ban]] imposed by [[Governor of Florida|Florida Governor]] [[Ron DeSantis]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/desantis-school-mask-mandate-ban-unlawful-florida-judge-rules-n1277788 (NBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois]]
****Reverend [[Jesse Jackson]] is transferred to a rehab facility, a week after being hospitalized for COVID-19. His wife, [[Jacqueline Jackson]], remains in ICU. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jesse-jackson-covid-19-hospital-chicago/ (CBS News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio]]
****The [[United States Department of Agriculture|U.S. Department of Agriculture]] reports the world's first [[deer]] positive case of COVID-19 from white-tailed deer in the state of [[Ohio]].  [https://www.ctvnews.ca/health/coronavirus/u-s-reports-world-s-first-deer-with-covid-19-1.5564334 (CTV News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
***The [[Australian Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation]] recommends that children between the ages of 12 and 15 be included in the COVID-19 vaccination program using the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]]. Vaccination bookings for this age group will begin on September 13. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-08-27/atagi-advice-covid-vaccine-children-teenagers/100393160 (ABC News Australia)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]], [[Political impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**A federal prosecutor indicts President [[Alberto Fernández]] for violating the sanitary measures he himself decreed during a birthday celebration party for First Lady [[Fabiola Yáñez]] in July 2020. Fernández appeals to evade trial and volunteers to donate his salary. The prosecutors reject his proposal as they say that government officials cannot skip trial. [https://en.mercopress.com/2021/08/27/argentine-president-indicted-for-skipping-lockdown-pleas-to-buy-his-way-out-of-trial (MercoPress)]
*Former Mali leaders [[Bah Ndaw]] and [[Moctar Ouane]] are released from house arrest by the junta who removed them from power in May. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/malis-former-interim-president-pm-released-house-arrest-2021-08-27/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan–United States relations]]
**The [[Taliban]] [[Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan|regime]] appoints [[Khalil Haqqani]] as head of security in [[Kabul]]. Haqqani, a veteran of the [[Soviet–Afghan War]] and [[war on terror]], is a [[Specially Designated Global Terrorist|designated terrorist]] by the [[United States]], and is currently wanted on a US[[$]]5 million [[Bounty (reward)|bounty]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/national-security/new-taliban-head-security-kabul-wanted-u-s-terrorist-n1277700 (NBC News)]
*In a 73−50 vote, the [[Congress of Peru]] approves the leftist cabinet of [[President of Peru|President]] [[Pedro Castillo]], who thanked the Congress for "granting confidence". The vote increased the approval of Castillo's government, which currently holds a 38% approval rating. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/perus-congress-confirms-new-leftist-cabinet-2021-08-27/ (Reuters)]
